problem_motivation.content: Traditional processing techniques face challenges with refractory HEAs due to their high melting points.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques.

problem_motivation.content: Traditional superalloys cannot withstand extreme temperatures up to 3000°C, creating a need for new materials.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, for super high temperature conditions of up to 1500 °C and 3000 °C, traditional surperalloys are powerless.

problem_motivation.content: The need to use higher energy input to completely melt NbMoTaW powder and sufficiently shape the HEA due to its high melting point.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The melting point of NbMoTaW is higher than that of most common metal alloys. Therefore, a proper higher energy input with a combination of laser power and scanning velocity is important for melting the mixed powder completely and shaping the HEA sufficiently.

prior_approach.content: Senkov and others prepared a BCC refractory HEA (NbMoTaW) using vacuum arc-melting.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Accordingly, Senkov and others [ [11] , [12] ] prepared a body-centered cubic (BCC) structure refractory HEA with near-equiatomic concentrations, using NbMoTaW, which was produced by vacuum arc-melting.

prior_approach.content: Zhang et al. synthesized a refractory HEA coating using laser cladding.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Zhang et al. [ [14] ] synthesized a refractory HEA coating with composition close to TiZrNbWMo on C45 steel by laser cladding.

prior_approach.content: Joseph et al. fabricated an HEA using direct laser fabrication.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The Al 0.3 CoCrFeNi HEA was fabricated with direct laser fabrication by Joseph et al. [ [15] ]

prior_approach.content: Kunce and others synthesized HEAs using laser engineered net shaping (LENS).
prior_approach.evidence_span: Kunce and others [ [16] , [17] ] synthesized two HEAs, ZrTiVCrFeNi and TiZrNbMoV, from a blend of elemental powders near the equimolar ratio using laser engineered net shaping (LENS)

prior_approach.content: Prior work reports that as-cast NbMoTaW HEA exhibits brittleness with low plastic strain.
prior_approach.evidence_span: It has been reported that the as-cast NbMoTaW HEA is brittle with plastic strain ɛ p = 0.2%

prior_limitation.content: The ductility of NbMoTaW HEA at room temperature is low.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, the ductility of the NbMoTaW HEA at room temperature is low.

prior_limitation.content: Achieving full mixing of elements in refractory HEAs is challenging and difficult to process.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Furthermore, the full mixing of elements in the refractory HEAs is still a challenge.

prior_limitation.content: Traditional casting methods lack the high temperatures required for NbMoTaW and cannot form arbitrary shapes.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: For the casting process, the highest melting temperature is only 1800 °C, which is far from enough for the NbMoTaW alloy in this study. Besides, although the arc melting can go up to the melting point, this method cannot form an arbitrary shape.

prior_limitation.content: There are very few studies regarding the preparation of refractory HEA by SLM.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: There have been notably few studies regarding the preparation of refractory HEA by SLM.

prior_limitation.content: Manufacturing NbMoTaW HEA via traditional hot working remains a serious problem.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, the manufacturing of NbMoTaW HEA is still a serious problem for traditional hot working.

prior_limitation.content: The low plastic strain of the as-cast alloy limits its potential applications.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: which seriously limits its potential applications

causal_claim.content: The SLM process leads to a specific grain size of 13.4 μm.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The average grain size is 13.4 μm

causal_claim.content: Grain refinement in the SLM process significantly improves the hardness of the high-entropy alloy.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It can also be seen that grain refinement can significantly improve the hardness of high-entropy alloys

causal_claim.content: Elemental segregation forms corrosion couples, increasing the alloy's corrosion tendency.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This is because the existence of a small amount of composition segregation in the alloy as mentioned before, which is readily forming corrosion couples and makes the alloy more

causal_claim.content: The presence of passivating elements (Nb, Mo, Ta) contributes to the alloy's excellent corrosion resistance despite segregation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the elements Nb, Mo, and Ta contained in the alloy are all the easy passivation metals, which contributes to the excellent corrosion resistance

mechanism_principle.content: The improved plasticity and strength are attributed to the Hall-Petch relationship where decreasing grain size enhances these properties.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The well-known Hall–Petch (HP) law [ [22] , [23] ] illustrates the dependence of the grain size with the macroscopic plastic and the relationship between the brittle fracture stresses and polycrystal structure. Therefore, the plasticity, fatigue strength, and creep rate of the polycrystal BCC metal are improved when the grain size decreases

hypothesis_statement.content: The expectation that the material is suitable for marine engineering applications and must resist seawater corrosion.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Besides, this material is expected to be mainly used in the field of marine engineering; thus, it needs to resist seawater corrosion, which was tested in this study.

hypothesis_statement.content: The fine grain structure is expected to improve the mechanical properties of the final part.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The fine structure is thought to improve the mechanical properties of the final part

evidence_result.content: A single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was successfully formed using selective laser melting.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm.

evidence_result.content: The element with lower melting point and density exhibited a negative deviation in molar ratio of no more than 5%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy.

evidence_result.content: The HEA demonstrates superior microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance compared to traditional superalloys.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys

evidence_result.content: The average microhardness of the SLM-fabricated sample is 826 Hv, significantly higher than the constituent pure elements and superalloys.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the average microhardness value of the NbMoTaW HEA s (sintering by SLM) sample is 826 Hv

evidence_result.content: The NbMoTaW HEA sample has a free-corrosion current of 8.716 × 10^-11 A, which is two orders of magnitude lower than 316L steel.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the free-corrosion current of the HEA is reduced by two orders of magnitude compared with that of the 316 L steel

evidence_result.content: Visual inspection and weight loss measurements confirm that the NbMoTaW alloy suffers less corrosion damage than 316L steel under high voltage scanning.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Therefore, from the extent of lost weight, the NbMoTaW HEA also shows stronger corrosion resistance than does 316 L steel.

constraint.content: The design requirement for the oxygen content in the protective atmosphere to be below 20 ppm.
constraint.evidence_span: in a protective atmosphere of argon with an amount of oxygen under 20 ppm

constraint.content: The experimental design requirement that laser transmission is assumed not to occur in the metal powders for absorption calculation.
constraint.evidence_span: It can be assumed that transmission of the laser does not occur in metal powders
